answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Signed patent inventor record with patent office attestation. It demands a patent naming one inventor, granted years ago, and the glacier is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a patent naming one inventor, granted years ago — so privacy survives, and the canyon is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The ridge is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red.
